column1: # Capture -> TextMate scope prefixes that MEAN THE SAME THING.
# D3 ruling (2026-08-14): TextMate stays reasonably complete and is treated as
# the portable syntax format for consumers that will never run our extension —
# Linguist/GitHub being the concrete one. Per §7.4 the invariant is AGREEMENT,
# not disjointness:
#     TextMate may paint anything. Where both layers paint the same span, they
#     must agree. Overlap is fine; DISAGREEMENT is the bug.
# This file is what makes "agree" testable. It is not a third consumer mapping:
# TextMate scope names are themselves a shared, standard vocabulary (the same
# one Linguist consumes), so this is a vocabulary<->vocabulary correspondence and
# belongs beside captures.md rather than inside either editor.
# Format:  capture <TAB> space-separated allowed scope prefixes
# A span agrees if the TextMate scope starts with ANY listed prefix.
# ⭐ `*GENERIC*` lists TextMate scopes that mean "I have nothing more specific to
# say". Those NEVER count as disagreement, and the distinction is the whole
# point of the layering: TextMate cannot tell a definition name from a variable
# — `defn foo` and a reference to `foo` are the same regex — so `@function` over
# `variable.other` is the semantic layer ADDING information, not the two layers
# contradicting each other. In VS Code the semantic token wins anyway; for
# Linguist, `variable.other` is the honest limit of a regex grammar.
# A real disagreement is TextMate being CONFIDENTLY DIFFERENT: two specific
# scopes that cannot both be right.
# `property <- constant.other.keyword` is the same idea one step along: a map
# key in this language IS a keyword literal, so TextMate naming the LEXICAL
# class is correct and `@property` is the semantic layer adding the ROLE. Not
# two claims that cannot both be right. This is deliberately a per-capture
# allowance and NOT a *GENERIC* entry: `constant.other.keyword` against
# `@type.builtin` was a real TextMate mis-lex of `x:Int`, and making it
# generic would have hidden that.
*GENERIC*
attribute
character
comment
constant.builtin
constructor
function
keyword
module
number
operator
property
string
string.special.symbol
type
type.builtin
type.definition
variable
variable.hole
variable.logic
variable.parameter
